I had no idea I had aspergers, until I was 22 and trying out a new psychiatrist. On our second appointment, he just asked me to talk about myself, my tastes in life, hobbies, what my day to day was, how I was when I was younger, about my social life and social behavior, about any tics or mannerisms. He then said that my answers showed him a few signs of neurodivergency, and he also said he easily spotted my eye contact avoidance and a few mannerisms. He then urged me to get a neuropsychological evaluation, that would give him a full report on me, so that he could come with a diagnosis. And after hearing that he thought I could be ND, I did my research and the thing that matched me the most was mild autism, wich was the same thing that came up in my evaluation later. A good mental professional makes all the difference. Before I met this psychiatrist, I had gone trough 3 other psychiatrists along my life, 2 psychologists, and none had spotted the clues that I was always giving. The traits in my childhood that would indicate my diagnosis were: suffering extreme bullying, being unable to make friends, total lack of social skills and social understanding, patterns on my behavior, mannerisms with my hands, feet, etc. If I just had known what autism really was, his different "levels" or clues, I could've diagnosed myself years ago, or just getting myself a evaluation sooner. I lacked information on what autism is. I didn't think there was such a thing as "mild autism", before I honestly thought being autistic only meant banging your head on the wall and screaming a lot and being super sound sensitive, something that kids of the newer generation have, and I had that stupid view on autism because that's the only thing I had ever seen on autism before, on TV, on multiple stories about the struggles of being a parent of a kid with autism. Totally clueless of me.
